source.title: Harmonizing Multi-Objective LLM Unlearning via Unified Domain Representation and Bidirectional Logit Distillation
source.authors: Yisheng Zhong; Sijia Liu; Zhuangdi Zhu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including the appendix. Some table rows are flattened in the text, but their metric columns are identifiable from the headers and accompanying discussion.
record.tranche_reason: Tests prompt-based recovery after unlearning using adversarial prefilling attacks and reports attack success rates, a conceptual test of prompt-only recovery and resistance. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, or quantization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own benchmark results for target forgetting, general retention, and prefilling-attack success. It also discusses relearning and contextual attacks in related work, but those cited findings are not rows. Its tested prompt attack is adversarial prefilling; it does not test rephrasing, other languages, or in-context factual examples. No attack-success result for the base model or a model that never learned the target is reported.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own adversarial prefilling attacks, a prompt-only recovery attack, on many unlearned models and reports ASR against a base-model ASR. Those results bear on A and E. Its proposed distillation method is presented as robust to that attack, so the study also tests F. It does not test fine-tuning, internal edits or quantization.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude their data-standardization plus bidirectional logit distillation framework balances forgetting, utility, neighbor-domain retention and prefilling robustness. They say baselines suffer imbalanced trade-offs or superficial unlearning, e.g. MOLLM stays highly vulnerable (69.2% ASR). The stated headline ASR of 16.0% in the contributions conflicts with the tables (12.5% MUSE, 5.1% WMDP).
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes standardized QA training data and intention-prompted bidirectional top-K logit distillation. It evaluates prefilling robustness but does not reproduce the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization recovery procedures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by benchmark and unlearning method; reported ASR ranges from 1.5% to 69.2% on MUSE-Book and from 3.3% to 50.7% on WMDP-Cyber.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning methods cause over-refusal or accuracy loss on semantically neighboring domains (Obj2 Retain Acc, e.g. FLAT 42.7 and SFT 50.7 vs base 57.28 on MUSE).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning degrades knowledge on concepts adjacent to the forget target (over-refusal).

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient cosine similarity between unlearning objectives is near zero (0.04–0.08) with raw data formats and rises with QA standardization (Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heterogeneous data formats make multi-objective unlearning gradients near-orthogonal.

record.problems: The evaluated model/checkpoint names and sizes are not stated in the supplied experimental text. ASR is not reported for the Base Model, and there is no comparison to a model that never learned the target, so the claim's explicit false-condition cannot be assessed. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Target Forget is measured by ROUGE rather than accuracy, with no chance-level reference. The attack evaluation is limited to prefilling.
record.rows_left_out: Obj2 neighboring-domain retention, the aggregate overall-performance shift, and the ablation-table results were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure target recovery or prompt-attack resistance. MMLU was retained only for the proposed method and upper bound on each benchmark; the other methods' MMLU values are omitted to stay within the row limit and because General Retain is already recorded for those methods.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack; only cited in related work.
No activation ablation or analysis of access-blocking vs deletion.
Only adversarial prefilling is tested; rephrasing, other languages, other jailbreaks and in-context relearning are not.
The proposed method's robustness to fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization and non-prefilling prompts is untested.

missing.what: Base-model prefilling ASR: 70.5% on MUSE, 60.7% on WMDP-Cyber. It is the needed baseline for all ASR rows.
missing.locator: Table 1 and Table 3, Base Model row (flattened)

missing.what: Prefilling ASR for Obj1-only methods: GA 70.0%, SimNPO 70.5%, FLAT 39.0% (FLAT Forget 0.7).
MMLU for the other methods on MUSE: GA 36.45, SimNPO 60.40, FLAT 58.92, SFT 50.2, NGDiff 60.8, MOLLM 60.8, ET 60.3, DUET 49.9. Base is 60.8.
Ablation ASR: ours w/ DUET loss 12.5%, ours w/ BILD loss 23.5%.
The model used for the main experiments is not stated; only the gradient analysis names Llama 3.2 3B Instruct.

record.verdict_notes: The record wrongly says base ASR is not reported. The flattened tables give base ASR 70.5% (MUSE) and 60.7% (WMDP); the record misread these as base MMLU, whose true values are 60.8 and 59.9. SFT, NGDiff, MOLLM, DUET and the proposed method were trained with adversarial-prefix data, so their low ASR reflects a trained defense. GA, SimNPO and FLAT are the clean tests of prompt-only recovery. ET and the Upper Bound are in-context prompt-steering methods, not weight unlearning. Forget is measured by ROUGE; a near-zero ROUGE floor is used here as the near-chance analogue.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures target Forget with ROUGE rather than target accuracy and does not establish a chance-level reference. It does not compare attack success with a model that never learned the knowledge; the prompt attack tested is prefilling.
No fine-tuning or small-set relearning attack is performed.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion is reported.
Only adversarial prefilling is tested, not rephrasing, jailbreaks generally, other languages, or in-context information.
The proposed method is evaluated against prefilling attacks only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, and other prompt attacks is not tested.

relationships.condition: Obj1-only methods (GA, SimNPO, FLAT) on MUSE; MOLLM on MUSE; ET, SFT, NGDiff on WMDP-Cyber
relationships.reason: Prefilling ASR stays near the base ASR (70.5% MUSE, 60.7% WMDP). Values: MOLLM 69.2%, ET 50.7%, SFT 44.7%, NGDiff 40.0%. Per the text's Table 1, GA 70.0%, SimNPO 70.5% and FLAT 39.0% (FLAT despite Forget 0.7); those three are not yet rows (m-mollm-asr, w-et-asr, w-sft-asr, w-ngdiff-asr).
relationships.display_finding: Prefilling attack success on MUSE was 70.0% for GA, 70.5% for SimNPO, 39.0% for FLAT despite a Forget score of 0.7, and 69.2% for MOLLM, versus 70.5% for the base model; WMDP-Cyber rates were 50.7% for ET, 44.7% for SFT, and 40.0% for NGDiff, versus 60.7% for the base model.
